<ticket source="">
# # Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

**Type:** bug / error message

`POST /api/tasks` with `{}` answers `500` and `{"error": "Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1."}`. With `{"title": ""}` it creates an empty task. A body that is not JSON also answers a 500 with the parser's message. On the page, adding an empty task does nothing visible.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `POST /api/tasks` with a missing, empty or blank (only spaces) `title`, or a `title` that is not a string, answers `400` with `{"error": "title is required"}`, and no task is created.
2. The same rule applies to `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` when the body has a `title`.
3. A title longer than 200 characters (after trimming) answers `400` with `{"error": "title must be at most 200 characters"}`. Titles are saved trimmed.
4. A request body that is not valid JSON answers `400` with `{"error": "invalid JSON body"}`.
5. An unexpected error answers `500` with `{"error": "internal error"}` and never shows the internal message to the client (log it on the server instead).
6. When adding a task fails, the page shows the error message from the API.
7. Tests cover these cases.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Bug fix in two small, independent parts, plus a final check.

Back end (`src/app.ts`, `src/tasks.ts`, tests, README): today `POST /api/tasks` passes `body.title` straight to SQLite, `readJson` lets `JSON.parse` errors escape, and the catch-all sends `err.message` to the client. Plan: validate the title in one shared function. It must be a string, non-empty after trimming, and at most 200 characters after trimming. Failures give 400 `title is required` or `title must be at most 200 characters`, and the title is saved trimmed. POST always validates. PATCH validates only when the body has a `title` key, so `{"done": true}` still works, while `{"title": null}` or `{"title": 5}` gives 400. Invalid JSON gives 400 `invalid JSON body`. A valid JSON body that is not an object (`null`, `[]`, `5`) is treated as `{}`, so POST gives `title is required` rather than a crash. Any other error is logged on the server (`console.error`) and the client gets 500 `{"error": "internal error"}`. Tests go in `test/tasks.test.ts`, which already starts a server on a random port with an in-memory database. The README's error section is updated, since the public behaviour changes.

Front end (`public/app.js`): the form's submit handler has no error handling, so a rejected POST goes unseen. It will catch the failure and call the existing `show(err)`, which fills the `#error` element with the API's message. It will not clear the typed text on failure, and it clears the error after a success.

QA then checks each criterion against a running server, including the page, and adds any missing regression tests.

No blocking questions. The ticket does not say whether the 200-character limit counts UTF-16 units or characters. The plan uses `.length` after `trim()`.

tasks.goal: Harden the tasks API in `src/app.ts` and `src/tasks.ts`, with tests in `test/tasks.test.ts` and an update to `README.md`. (1) Add a `validateTitle(value: unknown): string` in `src/tasks.ts` that returns the trimmed title. It throws a small exported `HttpError` class (carrying `status` and `message`) with 400 `title is required` when the value is not a string or is empty or blank after `trim()`, and 400 `title must be at most 200 characters` when the trimmed length is over 200 (use `.length`). (2) In `src/app.ts`, `readJson` must throw `HttpError(400, 'invalid JSON body')` when `JSON.parse` fails. A parsed value that is not a plain object (null, array, number, string) is treated as `{}`. (3) POST calls `validateTitle(body.title)` before `createTask`, so a missing title gives 400 and creates nothing. PATCH calls `validateTitle` only when `Object.hasOwn(body, 'title')`, so `{done:true}` alone still works and `{title:null}` or `{title:5}` gives 400. Save the trimmed title. Validate before looking up the task, or keep 404 for unknown ids. Pick one and test it. (4) Replace the catch in `createServer` (`send(res, 500, { error: err.message })`) with a handler: for an `HttpError` send its status and `{ error: message }`; for anything else `console.error` the real error server-side and send 500 `{ error: 'internal error' }`. Never put `err.message` of a non-HttpError in a response. If headers were already sent, just end the response. (5) Tests, using the existing `call()` helper (add a way to send a raw non-JSON body for the invalid JSON case): POST with `{}`, `{title:''}`, `{title:'   '}`, `{title:5}`, `{title:null}` each gives 400 `title is required` and the list length is unchanged; a 200-character title is accepted, a 201-character one gives 400 with the length message; a title with surrounding spaces is saved trimmed (on POST and PATCH); PATCH with a bad title gives 400 and leaves the stored title unchanged; PATCH `{done:true}` still works; a raw body `{not json` on POST and on PATCH gives 400 `invalid JSON body`; an unexpected error gives 500 `internal error` with no internal text. To produce the unexpected error, force a real failure through the public API, or have `createServer` accept an optional injected route or db for the test. Silence or capture `console.error` in that test. (6) Update the README table and the line 'Errors answer { "error": "<message>" }' to list the 400 cases and their exact messages, and the 500 `internal error`. Contract with T2: the page reads `body.error` from non-2xx JSON responses, so every error response must be JSON `{ "error": string }`. Run `npm test`.

In `public/app.js`, make a failed add visible. The form `submit` handler (bottom of the file) awaits `api('/api/tasks', {method:'POST', ...})` with no error handling, so a rejection goes unseen. Wrap the POST and the following `render()` in try/catch and call the existing `show(err)` on failure, which writes the message into `#error`. The `api()` helper already throws `new Error(body.error)` for non-2xx JSON responses, so the text shown is the API's message (for example `title is required`). On failure keep what the user typed (do not call `form.reset()`); on success reset the form and clear the error text (`render()` already clears it). Contract with T1: error responses are JSON `{ "error": string }` with status 400 or 500; the server returns the exact messages `title is required`, `title must be at most 200 characters`, `invalid JSON body` and `internal error`. Check in `public/index.html` that the `#error` element is exposed to assistive tech (for example `role="alert"` or `aria-live`) and add that attribute only if it is missing; make no visual change otherwise. Also make `api()` robust when an error response has no JSON body (fall back to `res.statusText`). No new dependencies. Keep `form.reset()` from running when the request fails.

Once T1 and T2 are merged, check each acceptance criterion with evidence. Start the app with `npm start` on a free port, using the worktree's `$PORT` and an in-memory or temporary database, and use curl (`--fail-with-body` off, since 400 is expected) to confirm: POST `{}`, `{"title":""}`, `{"title":"   "}`, `{"title":5}` give 400 `title is required`; a 201-character title gives 400 `title must be at most 200 characters`; a padded title is stored trimmed; PATCH with a bad title gives 400; a non-JSON body gives 400 `invalid JSON body`; and no 500 response ever contains an internal message. Read `public/app.js` and, if a browser tool is available, submit an empty title on the page and confirm the API message shows in `#error`. Run `npm test` and confirm that every case above is covered by a test in `test/tasks.test.ts`. Add only the missing regression tests. Stop every process you started.

reviews.summary:
I found nothing that must change. I read the full diff against the base (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js, README.md, test/tasks.test.ts) and ran `npm test`: 28 pass, 0 fail.

- **AC1–AC3 (title rules):** `validateTitle` rejects non-strings and empty or blank titles with 400 `title is required`. It rejects trimmed titles over 200 characters with the length message, and returns the trimmed title. POST always validates it before creating. PATCH validates only when the body has a `title` key, and does so before the task lookup, which a test covers. `{done:true}` alone still works.
- **AC4 (bad JSON):** `readJson` throws 400 `invalid JSON body` when parsing fails. Valid JSON that is not an object is read as `{}`.
- **AC5 (internal errors):** the new `fail()` sends `HttpError`s as they are. Anything else is logged with `console.error` and answered 500 `internal error`. It only ends the response if headers were already sent. All error paths send JSON `{error: string}`. The 500 test breaks a database call through an injected opener. It checks the response hides the secret message and that the error was logged. The optional second argument of `createServer` that makes this possible is the seam the plan allowed.
- **AC6 (page):** the submit handler wraps the POST, `form.reset()` and `render()` in try/catch and calls `show(err)`. `form.reset()` is skipped on failure. `api()` falls back to `res.statusText` when the error body is not JSON. `index.html` already has `role="alert"` on `#error`, so it was correctly left alone.
- **AC7 (tests):** every case from the ticket is covered, and the tests go through the real HTTP interface. They are not mere restatements of the code.
- **Scope:** no unrelated changes. The README update matches the behaviour.

**Not checked:**
- I did not run the page in a browser, so AC6 is judged by reading `public/app.js`. No automated test covers it.
- There is no TypeScript compiler in the project, so I ran no typecheck.
- I did not run the new tests against the old code to see them fail.
- I did not exercise a live server myself.

public/app.js sends the title untrimmed. This is harmless because the server trims.

report.summary:
No exploitable vulnerabilities confirmed in the run's changes (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js).

Confirmed findings: none.

What I checked:
- A10:2025 (error handling): the catch-all now answers a generic 500 `internal error` and logs the real error server-side with console.error. The only error text sent to clients comes from HttpError, and its messages are fixed strings. The invalid-JSON handler does not echo the parser message. The headers-already-sent branch ends the response, so it does not fail open.
- Input validation: validateTitle rejects non-strings (null, number, object) and blank titles, trims, and caps length at 200. A body that is not a plain object is treated as `{}`, so `body.title` cannot throw on null. `Object.hasOwn` is safe for the parsed object. JSON.parse gives no prototype pollution through `__proto__` keys here, because only `title` and `done` are read.
- SQL: the queries are the existing parameterized statements. The title now reaches them only as a validated string. A bad `done` value (for example an object) on PATCH still fails inside SQLite, but it is now caught as a generic 500 with no leak. That is an input-validation gap, but the ticket puts it out of scope, and the result is only a log line.
- XSS (A05:2025): the page puts the API message into `error.textContent`, and task titles into `label.textContent`. There is no innerHTML. The `api()` change (`res.json().catch`) adds no risk.
- Dependencies (A03:2025): package.json has no dependencies and the diff adds none, so there is nothing for an audit to flag.
- The injectable `open` parameter in createServer is only called by the code that creates the server. No request input reaches it.

What I did not check: I ran no live server and no tests. I did not test the 500 path live. The rest of the app (db.ts, main.ts, static serving) was only read where the diff touches it. I did not review the tests or the README. Authentication, rate limiting and body size limits are absent and out of scope for the ticket.
out_of_scope_findings: No request body size limit: readJson buffers the whole body in memory, so a large POST can exhaust memory (A06:2025/A02:2025 hardening, DoS). The ticket excludes it.
PATCH `done` is not validated: a non-primitive value gives a generic 500 and a logged error instead of a 400. The ticket excludes it.
No authentication or rate limiting on the API (excluded by the ticket).
